raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview


Add [HALOps](https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/HALOps) as an opt-in MXFP8 W8A8 dense-GEMM backend for Blackwell (SM100), selected with `--linear-backend halops`. An MXFP8 MegaMoE online-quantization path lets a BF16 checkpoint run with MXFP8 experts (canonical per-32 UE8M0 scales) without pre-quantized expert weights or scales.

## Claims


- New opt-in `halops` linear backend: W8A8 MXFP8 `dense_gemm` plus the fused `group_wise_quant` activation quantizer, wrapped in one CUDA-graph-safe custom op. Defaults are unchanged: `auto` keeps HALOps last in the CUDA MXFP8 priority list and the package is imported lazily.
- Accuracy parity with the DeepGEMM dense MXFP8 baseline on the full GSM8K test set (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy): 0.884 / 0.889 / 0.8787 vs. 0.873 / 0.8757 / 0.8802.
- End-to-end throughput within 0.96–1.02× of the DeepGEMM baseline at concurrency 1–64 for both 1k-in/256-out and 4k-in/1k-out workloads.
- Ships as an optional extra (`vllm[halops]`) with a documentation page and CPU unit tests (21 passed).

## Validation


**Unit tests**

```bash
python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/kernels/test_halops_linear.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mega_moe_online_quant.py -v   # 21 passed
```

**Accuracy** 
DeepSeek-V4-Flash, full GSM8K test set (1319 questions), 5-shot, greedy, `--max-tokens 2048`, TP4 + EP. The two arms differ only in `--linear-backend`; MoE is MXFP8 MegaMoE in both.

| arm | `--linear-backend` | GSM8K (3 runs) |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| HALOps | `halops` | 0.884 / 0.889 / 0.8787 |
| DeepGEMM | `deep_gemm` | 0.873 / 0.8757 / 0.8802 |

The DeepGEMM dense MXFP8 kernel used as the baseline was written for this comparison and is not part of this PR.

**Speed**
4 SM100 GPU, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4 + EP, online MXFP8 quantization. Attention dense MXFP8 GEMM is the only variable: MoE is `deep_gemm_mega_moe` in both arms and they differ only in `--linear-backend`.

Dataset level (`vllm bench serve`, random 1024 in / 256 out, `--ignore-eos`, prefix caching disabled, median of 3 runs):

| concurrency | HALOps out tok/s | DeepGEMM out tok/s | ratio | mean TTFT, HALOps / DeepGEMM (ms) | mean TPOT, HALOps / DeepGEMM (ms) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 113.4 | 117.7 | 0.964 | 169.6 / 178.4 | 8.18 / 7.83 |
| 8 | 749.9 | 766.5 | 0.978 | 312.8 / 335.7 | 9.47 / 9.17 |
| 64 | 3807.5 | 3789.7 | 1.005 | 539.4 / 572.4 | 14.75 / 14.70 |

4k in / 1k out, 2 paired repeats:

| concurrency | HALOps out tok/s | DeepGEMM out tok/s | ratio |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 117.35 / 117.62 | 121.98 / 122.14 | 0.962–0.963 |
| 8 | 770.12 / 773.57 | 786.99 / 787.00 | 0.979–0.983 |
| 32 | 2267.42 / 2284.26 | 2270.51 / 2268.92 | 0.999–1.007 |
| 64 | 3612.99 / 3686.30 | 3615.29 / 3614.85 | 0.999–1.020 |

Reproduce the serving configuration (DeepSeek-V4-Flash BF16, online MXFP8, HALOps dense GEMM and MXFP8 MegaMoE):

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --quantization mxfp8 \
  --quantization-config '{"ignore": ["*.wo_a"]}' \
  --linear-backend halops \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --port 30082
```

## Details


**Motivation.** [HALOps](https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/HALOps) is the PaddlePaddle team's high-performance kernel library for NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100). vLLM already serves MXFP8 dense linears through FlashInfer, Marlin, Torch and b12x; this PR adds HALOps as another explicitly selected backend while leaving every default untouched (`auto` keeps it last in the CUDA MXFP8 priority order).

**Packaging.** The `halops` wheel is published on PaddlePaddle's CUDA 13.2 index rather than PyPI, so it cannot be a hard wheel dependency (`pip install vllm` would fail without that index). It is an optional extra:

```bash
uv pip install "vllm[halops]" \
  -f https://www.paddlepaddle.org.cn/packages/stable/cu132/halops/
```

**Changes.**

- `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/halops.py` (new): `HALOpsMxfp8LinearKernel` with a lazy `halops` loader and install hint, SfAtom weight-scale swizzle at load time, and `group_wise_quant` + `dense_gemm` wrapped in one custom op with a fake impl (CUDA-graph safe).
- `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py`: register the kernel in `_POSSIBLE_MXFP8_KERNELS[CUDA]` (last) and `_LINEAR_BACKEND_KERNEL_MAP["halops"]`.
- `vllm/config/kernel.py`: add `"halops"` to the `LinearBackend` literal and its docstring.
- `setup.py`, `requirements/halops.txt`, `docs/features/quantization/halops.md`: optional extra, pinned standalone requirement, and a backend page with supported configurations.
- `tests/model_executor/kernels/test_halops_linear.py` (CPU): registration, `--linear-backend halops` selection and fallback, `can_implement()` limits, weight preparation, custom-op registration, and the `apply_weights` call shape, with a stand-in for the `halops` package.
- `docs/features/quantization/README.md`: link the new backend page from the supported-formats list.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+# HALOps Linear Backend
+
+[HALOps](https://www.paddlepaddle.org.cn/packages/stable/cu132/halops/) provides
+high-performance MXFP8 W8A8 GEMM kernels for NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100) GPUs. It is
+published on the PaddlePaddle package index instead of PyPI, so it is an opt-in
+extra and is never part of vLLM's default install.
+
+## Installation
+
+```bash
+uv pip install "vllm[halops]" \
+    -f https://www.paddlepaddle.org.cn/packages/stable/cu132/halops/
+```
+
+The same pin is available as a standalone requirements file:
+
+```bash
+pip install -r requirements/halops.txt
+```
+
+`--find-links` adds a wheel location rather than an index, and the page hosts
+only `halops` wheels, so resolution for every other package is unchanged. The
+published wheels target CUDA 13.2 (`cu132`); use the `-f` URL that matches the
+CUDA build of your `torch`.
+
+## Usage
+
+Select the backend explicitly:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve <model> --linear-backend halops
+```
+
+`halops` only implements MXFP8 linear layers. Other quantization schemes and
+layer types fall back to automatic selection. Automatic selection treats HALOps
+as the last MXFP8 candidate, after the established backends, so pass
+`--linear-backend halops` to actually use it.
+
+## Supported Configurations
+
+| Backend | Supported configurations |
+| ------- | ------------------------ |
+| Linear | MXFP8 W8A8: `fp8_e4m3` weights and activations with per-1x32 `e8m0` block scales, `K` and `N` divisible by 128 |
+
+The backend requires a Blackwell (SM100) device.
+
+If the `halops` package is not importable, `--linear-backend halops` fails with
+an actionable error, and automatic selection skips the backend.

+# file, so the PaddlePaddle find-links location below never leaks into vLLM's
+# default resolution and `pip install vllm` stays resolvable from PyPI alone.

+#   pip install -r requirements/halops.txt

@@ -0,0 +1,295 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""HALOps MXFP8 linear backend: registration, backend selection, shape gating,
+weight preparation and the custom-op boundary.
+
+The `halops` wheel is only published for Blackwell, so all but the
+weight-preparation test stand in for the package in `sys.modules` and run on
+CPU.
+"""
+
+import sys
+import types
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.config.kernel import KernelConfig
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear import (
+    _LINEAR_BACKEND_KERNEL_MAP,
+    _POSSIBLE_MXFP8_KERNELS,
+    HALOpsMxfp8LinearKernel,
+    Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig,
+    TorchMxFp8LinearKernel,
+    _resolve_backend_kernels,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.mxfp8 import halops as halops_mod
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp8_utils import (
+    MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE,
+    swizzle_mxfp8_scale,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import PlatformEnum, current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test
+
+
+def test_halops_is_registered_last_in_the_cuda_mxfp8_priority_list() -> None:
+    """`auto` keeps preferring every other CUDA MXFP8 kernel."""
+    assert HALOpsMxfp8LinearKernel in _LINEAR_BACKEND_KERNEL_MAP["halops"]
+    assert _POSSIBLE_MXFP8_KERNELS[PlatformEnum.CUDA][-1] is HALOpsMxfp8LinearKernel
+
+
+def test_linear_backend_halops_selects_the_halops_kernel() -> None:
+    """`--linear-backend halops` narrows MXFP8 selection to HALOps."""
+    config = VllmConfig(kernel_config=KernelConfig(linear_backend="halops"))
+
+    with set_current_vllm_config(config):
+        selected = _resolve_backend_kernels(
+            _POSSIBLE_MXFP8_KERNELS[PlatformEnum.CUDA],
+            "MXFP8",
+            quantization="mxfp8",
+        )
+
+    assert selected == [HALOpsMxfp8LinearKernel]
+
+
+def test_linear_backend_halops_falls_back_for_other_layer_types() -> None:
+    """A layer type HALOps does not implement keeps automatic selection."""
+    config = VllmConfig(kernel_config=KernelConfig(linear_backend="halops"))
+
+    with set_current_vllm_config(config):
+        selected = _resolve_backend_kernels(
+            [TorchMxFp8LinearKernel], "MXFP8", quantization="mxfp8"
+        )
+
+    assert selected == [TorchMxFp8LinearKernel]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("config", "reason"),
+    [
+        (
+            Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig(weight_shape=(128, 128), bmm_batch_size=2),
+            "HALOps dense_gemm does not implement grouped BMM.",
+        ),
+        (
+            Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig(weight_shape=(128, 64)),
+            "HALOps requires K divisible by 128, got 64.",
+        ),
+        (
+            Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig(weight_shape=(64, 128)),
+            "HALOps requires N divisible by 128, got 64.",
+        ),
+    ],
+)
+def test_halops_rejects_unsupported_layer_configs(config, reason) -> None:
+    assert HALOpsMxfp8LinearKernel.can_implement(config) == (False, reason)
+
+
+def test_halops_accepts_128_aligned_matmul() -> None:
+    assert HALOpsMxfp8LinearKernel.can_implement(
+        Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig(weight_shape=(256, 512))
+    ) == (True, None)
+
+
+def test_missing_halops_package_names_the_install_command(monkeypatch) -> None:
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "halops", None)
+
+    with pytest.raises(ImportError, match=r'uv pip install "vllm\[halops\]" -f'):
+        halops_mod._import_halops()
+
+
+requires_halops_sm100 = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not HALOpsMxfp8LinearKernel.is_supported()[0],
+    reason="needs a Blackwell (SM100) GPU with the halops wheel installed",
+)
+
+
+def _make_layer(n: int, k: int) -> torch.nn.Module:
+    layer = torch.nn.Module()
+    weight = torch.randn(n, 2 * k).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)[:, ::2]
+    assert not weight.is_contiguous()
+    layer.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(weight, requires_grad=False)
+    layer.weight_scale = torch.nn.Parameter(
+        torch.randint(0, 256, (n, k // MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE), dtype=torch.uint8),
+        requires_grad=False,
+    )
+    return layer
+
+
+@requires_halops_sm100
+def test_halops_weight_preparation_swizzles_scales_and_keeps_loaders() -> None:
+    """Loaded weights must stay reloadable by the weight cache daemon."""
+    n, k = 128, 256
+    layer = _make_layer(n, k)
+    expected_weight = layer.weight.detach().contiguous()
+    expected_scale = swizzle_mxfp8_scale(
+        layer.weight_scale.detach().clone(), M=n, K=k
+    ).view(n, k // MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE)
+    weight_loader, scale_loader = object(), object()
+    layer.weight.weight_loader = weight_loader
+    layer.weight_scale.weight_loader = scale_loader
+    kernel = HALOpsMxfp8LinearKernel(Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig(weight_shape=(n, k)))
+
+    kernel.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+
+    assert layer.weight.is_contiguous()
+    assert torch.equal(
+        layer.weight.view(torch.uint8), expected_weight.view(torch.uint8)
+    )
+    assert layer.weight_scale.shape == (n, k // MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE)
+    assert layer.weight_scale.dtype == torch.uint8
+    torch.testing.assert_close(layer.weight_scale, expected_scale)
+    assert layer.weight.weight_loader is weight_loader
+    assert layer.weight_scale.weight_loader is scale_loader
+    assert layer.weight_block_size == [1, MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE]
+
+
+class _FakeHalops(types.ModuleType):
+    """Stand-in for the external `halops` package; records the kernel's calls."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__("halops")
+        self.quant_calls: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, str, bool]] = []
+        self.gemm_calls: list[dict] = []
+
+    def group_wise_quant(self, x: torch.Tensor, *, mode: str, use_swizzle: bool):
+        self.quant_calls.append((x, mode, use_swizzle))
+        m, k = x.shape
+        m_sf = (m + 127) // 128 * 128
+        return (
+            torch.empty((m, k), dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device=x.device),
+            torch.zeros((m_sf, k // 32), dtype=torch.uint8, device=x.device),
+        )
+
+    def dense_gemm(self, **kwargs) -> None:
+        self.gemm_calls.append(kwargs)
+        kwargs["output"].fill_(3.0)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def fake_halops(monkeypatch) -> _FakeHalops:
+    fake = _FakeHalops()
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "halops", fake)
+    return fake
+
+
+def _weights(n: int = 128, k: int = 64):
+    return (
+        torch.empty((n, k), dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn),
+        torch.zeros((n, k // MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE), dtype=torch.uint8),
+    )
+
+
+def test_halops_linear_quantizes_activations_and_passes_weight_scales(
+    fake_halops,
+) -> None:
+    """The output keeps the real M; only the SfAtom scales are padded."""
+    weight, weight_scale = _weights()
+    x = torch.randn((2, 3, 64), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    bias = torch.ones(128, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+    out = halops_mod._halops_mxfp8_linear(x, weight, weight_scale, bias)
+
+    assert len(fake_halops.quant_calls) == 1
+    (gemm,) = fake_halops.gemm_calls
+    assert gemm["output"].shape == (6, 128)
+    assert gemm["bias"] is bias
+    assert gemm["sfb"] is weight_scale
+    assert gemm["alpha"] is None
+    assert gemm["sm_count"] == -1
+    assert gemm["mode"] == "w8a8-mxfp8"
+    assert out.shape == (2, 3, 128)
+    assert out.dtype is torch.bfloat16
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out, torch.full_like(out, 3.0))
+
+
+def test_halops_linear_without_bias_passes_none(fake_halops) -> None:
+    weight, weight_scale = _weights()
+
+    halops_mod._halops_mxfp8_linear(
+        torch.randn((1, 64), dtype=torch.bfloat16), weight, weight_scale, None
+    )
+
+    assert fake_halops.gemm_calls[0]["bias"] is None
+
+
+def test_halops_linear_zero_tokens_skips_the_kernel(fake_halops) -> None:
+    weight, weight_scale = _weights()
+
+    out = halops_mod._halops_mxfp8_linear(
+        torch.empty((0, 64), dtype=torch.bfloat16), weight, weight_scale, None
+    )
+
+    assert out.shape == (0, 128)
+    assert fake_halops.quant_calls == []
+    assert fake_halops.gemm_calls == []
+
+
+def test_halops_linear_quantizes_a_contiguous_copy(fake_halops) -> None:
+    weight, weight_scale = _weights()
+    storage = torch.randn((4, 128), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    x = storage[:, ::2]
+    assert not x.is_contiguous()
+
+    out = halops_mod._halops_mxfp8_linear(x, weight, weight_scale, None)
+
+    q_input, mode, use_swizzle = fake_halops.quant_calls[0]
+    assert q_input.is_contiguous()
+    assert torch.equal(q_input, x)
+    assert mode == "w8a8-mxfp8"
+    assert use_swizzle
+    assert out.dtype is torch.bfloat16
+
+
+def test_halops_linear_upcasts_fp32_activations(fake_halops) -> None:
+    weight, weight_scale = _weights()
+    x = torch.randn((4, 64), dtype=torch.float32)
+
+    out = halops_mod._halops_mxfp8_linear(x, weight, weight_scale, None)
+
+    q_input = fake_halops.quant_calls[0][0]
+    assert q_input.dtype is torch.bfloat16
+    assert q_input.shape == (4, 64)
+    assert out.dtype is torch.float32
+
+
+def test_halops_custom_op_dispatches_to_the_kernel(fake_halops) -> None:
+    """The op is registered on the platform dispatch key, not `Composite`."""
+    if not current_platform.is_cuda():
+        pytest.skip("the custom op is registered for the CUDA dispatch key")
+    weight, weight_scale = (t.cuda() for t in _weights())
+    x = torch.randn((4, 64), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+
+    out = torch.ops.vllm.halops_mxfp8_linear(x, weight, weight_scale, None)
+
+    assert out.shape == (4, 128)
+    assert len(fake_halops.gemm_calls) == 1
+
+
+def test_halops_custom_op_fake_impl_matches_the_real_shape() -> None:
+    weight, weight_scale = _weights()
+    x = torch.empty((2, 3, 64), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+    out = halops_mod._halops_mxfp8_linear_fake(x, weight, weight_scale, None)
+

+    assert out.dtype is torch.bfloat16
+    assert out.device == x.device
+
+
+def test_halops_custom_op_is_registered_with_a_fake_impl() -> None:
+    from torch._subclasses.fake_tensor import FakeTensorMode
+
+    schema = str(torch.ops.vllm.halops_mxfp8_linear.default._schema)
+    assert "halops_mxfp8_linear" in schema
+    assert "Tensor? bias" in schema

+    with FakeTensorMode():

+        x = torch.empty((2, 3, 64), dtype=torch.bfloat16)

+    assert out.shape == (2, 3, 128)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""MXFP8 W8A8 linear kernel backed by HALOps' ``dense_gemm``."""
+
+import torch
+from torch.nn.parameter import Parameter
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp8_utils import (
+    MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE,
+    swizzle_mxfp8_scale,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.utils import replace_parameter
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import direct_register_custom_op
+
+from .Mxfp8LinearKernel import Mxfp8LinearKernel, Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+# dense_gemm reads K in whole 128-element blocks and its SfAtom scale layout is
+# 128-row aligned on both operands.
+HALOPS_ALIGN = 128
+HALOPS_MODE = "w8a8-mxfp8"
+
+
+def _import_halops():
+    try:
+        from halops import dense_gemm, group_wise_quant
+    except ImportError as exc:
+        raise ImportError(
+            "HALOps GEMM backend requested, but the `halops` package is not "
+            "installed. Install it with "
+            '`uv pip install "vllm[halops]" -f '
+            "https://www.paddlepaddle.org.cn/packages/stable/cu132/halops/`; "
+            "the find-links URL must match the CUDA build of torch."
+        ) from exc
+    return dense_gemm, group_wise_quant
+
+
+def _halops_mxfp8_linear(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    weight_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    n, k = weight.shape
+    out_dtype = x.dtype
+    x2d = x.reshape(-1, k)
+    if x2d.dtype not in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16):
+        x2d = x2d.to(torch.bfloat16)
+    m = x2d.shape[0]
+    if m == 0:
+        return x.new_empty((*x.shape[:-1], n))
+    x2d = x2d.contiguous()
+
+    dense_gemm, group_wise_quant = _import_halops()
+    q_input, sfa = group_wise_quant(x2d, mode=HALOPS_MODE, use_swizzle=True)
+
+    output = torch.empty((m, n), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=x.device)
+    dense_gemm(
+        input=q_input,
+        weight=weight,
+        sfa=sfa,
+        sfb=weight_scale,
+        output=output,
+        bias=None if bias is None else bias.to(torch.bfloat16),
+        alpha=None,
+        sm_count=-1,
+        mode=HALOPS_MODE,
+    )
+    return output.to(out_dtype).view(*x.shape[:-1], n)
+
+
+def _halops_mxfp8_linear_fake(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    weight_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.empty((*x.shape[:-1], weight.shape[0]), dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
+
+
+direct_register_custom_op(
+    op_name="halops_mxfp8_linear",
+    op_func=_halops_mxfp8_linear,
+    fake_impl=_halops_mxfp8_linear_fake,
+)
+
+
+class HALOpsMxfp8LinearKernel(Mxfp8LinearKernel):
+    """MXFP8 W8A8 GEMM via HALOps ``dense_gemm`` (SM100)."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def is_supported(
+        cls, compute_capability: int | None = None
+    ) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
+        if not current_platform.is_cuda():
+            return False, "HALOps dense_gemm requires a CUDA device."
+        if not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100):
+            return False, "HALOps dense_gemm requires Blackwell (SM100)."
+        try:
+            _import_halops()
+        except ImportError as exc:
+            return False, str(exc)
+        return True, None
+
+    @classmethod
+    def can_implement(cls, c: Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
+        if c.bmm_batch_size is not None:
+            return False, "HALOps dense_gemm does not implement grouped BMM."
+        n, k = c.weight_shape
+        if k % HALOPS_ALIGN != 0:
+            return (
+                False,
+                f"HALOps requires K divisible by {HALOPS_ALIGN}, got {k}.",
+            )
+        if n % HALOPS_ALIGN != 0:
+            return (
+                False,
+                f"HALOps requires N divisible by {HALOPS_ALIGN}, got {n}.",
+            )
+        return True, None
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        weight = layer.weight.data  # [N, K]
+        n, k = weight.shape
+        scale = layer.weight_scale.data
+        assert weight.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn and weight.ndim == 2, (
+            f"HALOps MXFP8 expects an fp8 2D weight, got "
+            f"{weight.dtype} {tuple(weight.shape)}."
+        )
+        expected = (n, k // MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE)
+        assert tuple(scale.shape) == expected, (
+            f"HALOps MXFP8 expects per-32 weight scales {expected}, got "
+            f"{tuple(scale.shape)}."
+        )
+        # dense_gemm consumes the uint8 SfAtom layout that group_wise_quant
+        # emits for weights; vLLM's swizzle is bit-identical to it.
+        n_padded = (n + HALOPS_ALIGN - 1) // HALOPS_ALIGN * HALOPS_ALIGN
+        sfb = swizzle_mxfp8_scale(scale, M=n, K=k).view(n_padded, k // MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE)
+        replace_parameter(
+            layer, "weight", Parameter(weight.contiguous(), requires_grad=False)
+        )
+        replace_parameter(layer, "weight_scale", Parameter(sfb, requires_grad=False))
+        layer.weight_block_size = [1, MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE]
+
+    def apply_weights(
+        self,
+        layer: torch.nn.Module,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        bias: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return torch.ops.vllm.halops_mxfp8_linear(
+            x, layer.weight, layer.weight_scale, bias
+        )
